info.title: Family OS Foundation API
info.description: Contract for the authorized account, family, membership, guardian-transfer, child roster, device lifecycle, safe zones, location telemetry, audit and readiness foundation. Every operation declared here is registered by the running server, and a CI drift gate fails the build when this document and app.js disagree in either direction. It still does not authorize deployment, account recovery, support operations, device control beyond the declared lifecycle, billing, AI, realtime or release claims.

tags.name: Guardian continuity
tags.description: Two-party primary-guardian transfer, not lost-account recovery.

tags.name: Safe zones
tags.description: Family-defined boundaries, readable by every member they apply to.

tags.name: Location
tags.description: Device-reported position, its honest acquisition state, and boundary crossings.

tags.name: Family chat
tags.description: Rooms as permissions: who is in a conversation is what decides who can read it, a message always has an author, and the only receipt stated is how many other participants have read up to a message.

get.summary: Check process liveness only

200.description: The process is running; this does not prove database, identity or schema readiness.

get.summary: Check configuration, database and reviewed schema readiness

200.description: Required configuration and PostgreSQL schema are ready.

503.description: At least one required dependency or configuration is not ready; no protected capability should be claimed.

get.summary: Discover only the verified principal's active families
get.description: The server derives eligible families from the verified principal. This read accepts no query parameters and returns no partial result when the bounded discovery limit is exceeded.

200.description: Minimal active-family discovery envelope, or an empty envelope when the verified principal has no eligible family.

post.summary: Create a family with the verified principal as active primary guardian

201.description: Family created or durable idempotent replay returned.

get.summary: Read a family only as an active family member

200.description: Family membership envelope.

get.summary: Read the verified guardian's durable children roster
get.description: Only active guardian memberships can read this parent control-centre roster. Device, location and policy state are deliberately outside this roster endpoint.

200.description: Durable child profile roster, including an empty roster.

post.summary: Create one durable child profile as the active primary guardian
post.description: This creates only a durable family roster profile, including its selected avatar emoji and named theme swatch. It does not create a child login, pair a device, report location, or apply a policy.

201.description: Child profile created or durable idempotent replay returned.

get.summary: Read linked family devices and their latest telemetry as an active guardian
get.description: Returns only the latest stored telemetry for linked devices. It is not a location history endpoint and makes no claim about background collection freshness beyond lastSeenAt.

200.description: Linked devices with their latest authorized telemetry.

post.summary: Link one device to an existing child profile as the active primary guardian
post.description: Phase 1 registration is guardian-authorized. A device credential or Android background service is not created by this endpoint.

201.description: Device linked or durable idempotent replay returned.

post.summary: Create an expiring one-time child-device pairing code as the active primary guardian
post.description: The raw pairing code is returned once, while the server retains only its digest. It must be claimed by a child device before expiry.

201.description: One-time pairing capability created.

post.summary: Claim a one-time pairing code from a child device
post.description: This unauthenticated bootstrap endpoint is IP-rate-limited. A successful response returns a device credential once; the code cannot be claimed again.

201.description: Device paired and device credential issued once.

post.summary: Store one linked device latest telemetry update
post.description: Accepts latest telemetry from an active primary guardian during controlled support operations or from the paired child device using its Device capability. The device capability is not a guardian bearer token.

200.description: Latest telemetry accepted.

get.summary: What the family agreed to do together, inside a window
get.description: The events whose start falls inside [from, to), with their audience, the answers given and what has been recorded as attended. Cancelled events are included with their reason and their author: the plan changed, and a child is owed the reason rather than a gap in the calendar.

parameters.name: from
parameters.description: The first instant of the window, inclusive.

parameters.name: to
parameters.description: The end of the window, exclusive. At most 400 days after `from`.

200.description: The events in the window.

post.summary: States an event and who it is for
post.description: The audience is stated here, in the same request, because an event nobody is invited to is a note rather than a plan. `reminderMinutes` records what the family asked for; this contract never claims a notification was delivered, because nothing here can know that.

201.description: The event as stored, with its audience.

422.description: The event is stated in the past, or longer than a month.

patch.summary: Changes a plan, stating the version that was read
patch.description: Two guardians editing the same evening must collide loudly rather than silently overwrite each other, so the body carries the `version` the client read and a mismatch is a 409. A child who has already answered or attended cannot be removed from the audience: their answer is a record with an author, and this route will not delete it silently.

200.description: The event after the change.

409.description: The version is stale, the event was cancelled, or a name being removed has already answered.

422.description: The change would end the event before it starts.

post.summary: Calls an event off, with a reason and an author
post.description: A cancellation is not a deletion: the row keeps its times, its audience and its answers, and gains the membership that called it off, the reason they gave and the moment they gave it. Cancelling twice is refused rather than ignored, because silence would let two guardians each believe they were the one who called it off.

200.description: The cancelled event.

post.summary: Records what actually happened, after the event started
post.description: Attendance is a fact with an author and a moment, written by a guardian. Recording it before the event has started is refused (`event_not_started`) because that would be storing a promise about a person, and recording it on a cancelled event is refused because there is nothing to have attended. Nothing in this route infers attendance from a device.

200.description: The attendance record as stored.

409.description: The event has not started yet, or it was cancelled.

post.summary: Records the answer a child gave in words
post.description: For a child who spoke to a guardian instead of tapping their own phone. The author of the stored answer is the guardian who recorded it, and the request cannot say otherwise: exactly one author per answer is a database constraint, not a convention. A `declined` answer is stored with the same weight as an `accepted` one - a calendar that counts only yes is a scoreboard.

200.description: The answer as stored.

409.description: The event was cancelled or has already started.

get.summary: The child's own invitations, from their own handset
get.description: The events this child is invited to, with their own answer and what has been recorded about their attendance - and deliberately without any sibling's answer, because a child's phone has no business knowing whether their brother said no. No child id appears in the path: the credential issued at pairing is what proves which child is asking.

200.description: This child's invitations in the window.

post.summary: The child's own answer
post.description: A handset answers for the child it is paired with and for nobody else: the child is read from the device row, and the audience row must exist for that child, so answering on a sibling's behalf is refused by storage rather than by a check somebody could remove. The answer window closes when the event starts, at which point the question becomes what attendance records are for.

200.description: The answer as stored.

409.description: The event was cancelled or has already started.

get.summary: List the family's memberships as the caller is allowed to see them
get.description: Every membership of the family, ordered by status group then age, with isSelf decided on the server against the authenticated principal. The invitee's subject is deliberately not returned: a guardian does not need a durable identifier for a person to run a family.

200.description: The family membership roster.

post.summary: Primary guardian creates a pending co-guardian or child membership for a known OIDC subject
post.description: This Foundation endpoint does not send email, push or other invitation delivery. It does not expose a finished consumer invitation experience.

201.description: Pending membership created or durable idempotent replay returned.

post.summary: Accept a pending membership only as the exact nominated verified principal

200.description: Membership activated or durable idempotent replay returned.

post.summary: Revoke a pending invite or remove an active non-primary membership
post.description: Only the active primary guardian may perform this operation. Primary guardian removal requires the separate guardian continuity process.

200.description: Membership transitioned to revoked or removed; evidence remains durable.

post.summary: Request an expiry-bound transfer from current primary guardian to active co-guardian
post.description: This is not lost-account recovery, dispute resolution, custody determination or a generic role edit.

201.description: Pending two-party transfer case created.

post.summary: Complete an unexpired guardian transfer only as the nominated active co-guardian

200.description: The family primary reference and both guardian roles changed atomically.

post.summary: Cancel a pending guardian transfer only as its initiating current primary guardian

200.description: Transfer cancelled with durable evidence.

get.summary: List the current guardian-scoped minimum audit envelope

200.description: Maximum one hundred newest minimum audit envelope entries.

get.summary: Read the server-owned permission explanation for the acting membership
get.description: The snapshot explains permission; it never grants it. The role is re-resolved from the durable membership on every call and each protected route re-checks authorization independently.

200.description: Versioned, expiring capability explanation for the acting membership role.

get.summary: List emitted AiEvent v1 facts for the family
get.description: Append-only, identifier-only facts observed by the server. Suggestions are not part of v1 and no entry can carry a payload, token or provider material.

200.description: Maximum one hundred newest emitted AiEvent v1 facts.

post.summary: Cut one child device off as the active primary guardian
post.description: The write half of the device lifecycle. Before this operation existed the server refused telemetry from a revoked credential with 401 but nothing could set the revocation, so a lost or stolen handset stayed trusted indefinitely. Idempotent: a retry with the same Idempotency-Key replays the first answer, and a second revocation under a different key is refused rather than overwriting who revoked the device and when. The response carries the device's derived condition so a guardian screen needs no second request.

requestBody.description: The reason is optional on purpose: cutting off a stolen handset is urgent, and a guardian forced to classify the loss first is a guardian who hesitates.

200.description: Device revoked, or the durable idempotent replay of that revocation.

get.summary: List the family's active safe zones
get.description: Every active zone with its geometry, its alert flags and the children it is assigned to. Readable by EVERY active member of the family, a child included: a boundary a person lives inside is not privileged information about them. Archived zones are not returned - a zone that has been taken out of service is not silently still being evaluated.

200.description: The active safe zones of this family.

post.summary: A guardian defines a safe zone for named children
post.description: Both geometry shapes are first-class: a circle is a centre and a radius, a polygon is an ordered ring of three to sixty-four points. The assignment is explicit and must name at least one child of THIS family, because a zone assigned to nobody reads like protection and evaluates like nothing at all. The zone starts at version 1 and every crossing records the version it was judged against. A child membership may not define a zone.

201.description: The zone as it was stored, or the durable idempotent replay of the same request.

get.summary: The live location picture, identical for every member of the family
get.description: Each child, each linked device, the newest reported fix, and where the child stands relative to each zone. THE SAME ROWS FOR EVERY ACTIVE MEMBER, a child included: this surface exists in the shape it does so that tracking can never be covert, and a monitoring state only one person can see is the anti-pattern this product refuses. Per device, `state` is `live`, `silent` or `never` - a device that stopped reporting and a device that has never reported are different answers and are kept different. Coordinates are null, never zero, when a fix carries none.

200.description: The family location snapshot.

get.summary: Recent safe-zone boundary crossings, newest first
get.description: The arrivals and departures the family is told about, capped at the hundred most recent. A crossing marked `baseline` is the FIRST time that child was ever observed relative to that zone: it is recorded so the next departure is a real crossing, and it triggers no alert, because "we had never looked before" is not "she just arrived". Same visibility rule as the live read.

200.description: The crossing feed.

post.summary: A child's device reports one position, and the server judges it
post.description: The device proves itself with the credential it was issued at pairing; a primary guardian may still report on its behalf while native collection is finished, and the audit record says which of the two happened. The server stores the fix, evaluates it against the zones ASSIGNED TO THAT CHILD, and answers with what it concluded: `evaluated` is false, with a `reason`, when the fix carried no usable position, when it arrived out of order (older than the newest fix already stored for that child - kept in the trail and deliberately NOT evaluated, so a late retry cannot replay history backwards), or when it was a duplicate. A duplicate - the same fix id, under this or a fresh key - produces no second row and no second crossing, which is what makes an arrival alert exactly-once. The `acquisition` state is an honesty switch enforced by both the request schema and the database: `located` and `stale_last_known` must carry coordinates and an accuracy, `acquiring` and `unavailable` must not carry any.

201.description: What the server stored and what it concluded.

patch.summary: A guardian changes which transitions a zone announces
patch.description: Only the two alert flags are writable here, and at least one of them must be sent. The boundary itself, its name and its assignment are deliberately not editable: a boundary that moves is a different boundary to anyone a crossing was already reported about. The zone's version moves with every change, because a crossing records the version it was judged against - turning arrival alerts off tonight must not make last night's announced arrival look like it happened under the new rule.

200.description: The zone with its new flags and its new version.

get.summary: The trail of one child, readable by every active member
get.description: The same rule as the live picture, for the same reason: one read, one rule for every active member of the family. A history only the parents could open would be the covert half of the same surface - a child able to see where she is now and not what was kept about her. Newest fix first, and a fix with no coordinates comes back with null coordinates rather than a zero: an acquiring answer is a fact about the device, and it must never be drawn as a position.

200.description: The child's trail, newest first, with the retention window it obeys.

get.summary: The family's emergency incidents, newest first
get.description: Open to every active member of the family, the child whose incident it is included: the same alert, the same recipients, the same delivery states. Selective visibility on an emergency is how a safety product quietly becomes a surveillance product. Each alert carries the honest delivery states of the press - `recorded` for what the in-app pipe will pick up, `not_configured` for what this build cannot send at all - and there is no state that claims a delivery nobody made.

parameters.name: status
parameters.description: `open` (default) lists what is still in flight, `resolved` what has ended, `all` everything.

200.description: The incidents, with their delivery rows.

get.summary: One incident, as the whole family may read it

200.description: The incident.

post.summary: A guardian opens an incident for a child
post.description: For the case where the handset is not the one in hand. The picture comes from the caller's device and is stored as it was; a second press while an incident is already open is refused with 409 `sos_alert_already_open` and the id of the incident that exists, because two open incidents would split the family's attention across two screens at the moment attention is the product.

201.description: The incident that was opened.

post.summary: The child's handset reports that the button was pressed
post.description: The device proves itself with the credential it was issued at pairing; a primary guardian may still report on its behalf while native collection is finished, and the audit record says which of the two happened. The child is the device's own child - a handset cannot speak for another - and the raiser is recorded as the device. The guardians of the family are the first rung, derived from the roster rather than from the request, and each of them gets an in-app delivery row (`recorded`) and a push row (`not_configured`, `push_transport_absent`): this build has no push transport and the row says so instead of claiming a message left the building.

201.description: The incident that was opened.

post.summary: A guardian says "I have seen this"
post.description: Acknowledging is not resolving and the two are separate acts: an incident that has been seen is still open, still escalating, still visible. A second acknowledgement - the other parent's tap, or a retry - reports the incident as it is rather than creating anything.

200.description: The incident, acknowledged.

post.summary: The incident climbs the family's own ladder
post.description: Rung 2 is the family's own verified contacts, in the family's own priority order. Only a `verified` contact is used - the same hard-skip law the client's escalation resolver enforces - and the answer reports how many were skipped for not being verified, so a parent finds that out now and not on the day it was needed. Escalation to a contact writes an `sms` delivery row in state `not_configured` with reason `sms_transport_absent`: the intent is recorded, and nothing claims a text was sent.

200.description: The incident and what the ladder did.

post.summary: A guardian closes the incident, stating why
post.description: The reason is required: a closed incident with no reason explains nothing. A child membership cannot close an incident here, and the refusal is a schema fact rather than a policy taste - nothing links a membership row to a child row, so the server cannot prove the incident is that account's. The child's own handset can, through its own route, and only as a false alarm.

200.description: The incident, closed.

post.summary: The child's handset closes its own incident as a false alarm
post.description: The handset that raised the incident is the only thing that can prove whose incident it is, and it may close it as `false_alarm` and with nothing else - the client's own cancel-own-SOS rule, held here so a client bug cannot turn "I pressed it by accident" into "my parent says it is over". A resolved incident answers a second call with the incident as it is, so a retry cannot be mistaken for a new act.

200.description: The incident, closed.

get.summary: The family's escalation ladder, in the family's order

200.description: Rung 2 and below.

post.summary: Add a rung to the family's ladder
post.description: The contact is created `unverified` and a ladder is bounded at eight contacts: a ladder longer than that is not a ladder anyone answers.

201.description: The contact as stored.

patch.summary: Verify, switch off, renumber or archive one rung
patch.description: Verification is a separate act from creation, and this is where it happens. Archiving takes a contact off the ladder without erasing the fact that it was once on it.

200.description: The contact as stored.

get.summary: What a child's phone may do right now, and why
get.description: The whole screen-time state in one read: the family's stored policy, today's countable minutes, the granted extension, the live instant lock, and the decision that follows - `free`, `limited` or `blocked` with a reason. The state is computed at the moment of the read from the policy, the usage rows and the family's own clock; nothing stores "blocked", so nothing can go stale. Guardians only: a child membership cannot be proven to be the subject of this read.

200.description: The server's answer, computed from the stored policy, today's minutes and the clock.

patch.summary: Sets a child's daily cap, school window and bedtime
patch.description: Only the fields that are sent change; the rest keep what the family already chose. Times are minutes east of UTC in the family's own offset, which is stored data rather than an assumption: a bedtime evaluated in the server's timezone would lock a child's phone in the middle of their afternoon. `expectedVersion` makes the write optimistic - a screen that read an older policy is refused with 409 instead of silently overwriting a decision someone else just made.

200.description: The server's answer, computed from the stored policy, today's minutes and the clock.

get.summary: The apps on a child's phone, each with the family's decision
get.description: The union of what the handset reported and what the family decided. An app the handset has and nobody has ruled on is `pending` - visible and undecided, never allowed by default. Each row carries today's minutes, whether it counts against the entertainment cap (education and free apps do not) and the same decision the state read would produce for it.

200.description: The server's answer, computed from the stored policy, today's minutes and the clock.

put.summary: Allows, frees, blocks or reopens one app
put.description: `allowed` counts against the daily cap and may carry its own limit; `free` is not counted at all; `blocked` is not usable whatever the clock says; `pending` puts the app back in front of a parent. A limit on an app that does not count is refused here and by the schema, because it would be a number no screen ever reads.

200.description: The server's answer, computed from the stored policy, today's minutes and the clock.

post.summary: Turns a child's phone off now, with a reason and an author
post.description: An instant lock is the one screen-time state that is stored rather than computed, because it is a decision a person made: it names the guardian and the reason, and it is released by another call. Pressing it twice finds the lock that exists instead of stacking a second one - one live lock per child is a partial unique index, not a check that races.

200.description: The server's answer, computed from the stored policy, today's minutes and the clock.

post.summary: Releases the live lock, and says whether there was one
post.description: Unlocking nothing is not an error: `released` reports honestly whether a lock was released, and the state that follows is computed as always. The released episode stays in the table, because "the phone was off from 21:10 to 07:00" is a fact a family will want tomorrow.

200.description: The server's answer, computed from the stored policy, today's minutes and the clock.

get.summary: The minutes a child asked for, and what the family answered
get.description: Newest first, with the family's clock settling what expired: a question nobody answered is reported as `expired` rather than as waiting for a parent three days later.

200.description: The server's answer, computed from the stored policy, today's minutes and the clock.

post.summary: A guardian asks for extra minutes on a child's behalf
post.description: The spoken version of the child's own request, recorded the same way - so a family that grants minutes over dinner has the same trail as one that approves them in the app. Requires a daily cap to extend: with no cap, "more minutes" is a number the server would never enforce.

201.description: The server's answer, computed from the stored policy, today's minutes and the clock.

post.summary: Approves minutes or denies the request, once
post.description: A guardian answers a question that is still open. Approving grants minutes that belong to the day the request named - the day's allowance is the sum of that day's approvals, so there is no wallet to drift. A request already decided or expired is a 409 rather than a silent second answer.

200.description: The server's answer, computed from the stored policy, today's minutes and the clock.

get.summary: The child's own phone asks what it may do
get.description: The same state block a guardian reads, computed by the same function from the same rows. The device credential proves which child this is, so this route takes no child id and never will: a parameter a client can choose is not proof of anything.

200.description: The server's answer, computed from the stored policy, today's minutes and the clock.

post.summary: The phone reports what it measured and what is installed, and may ask for more
post.description: Usage is cumulative for the day and the server keeps the greater of what is stored and what arrived, so a replay, a retry or a handset that reconnects after a day offline can neither reduce nor inflate the minutes a family is looking at. The inventory travels in the same call - an app nobody has ruled on becomes `pending` rather than silently allowed - and the request, when there is one, is recorded against the same clock and answered in the same response.

201.description: The server's answer, computed from the stored policy, today's minutes and the clock.

get.summary: The filter a child's phone must apply
get.description: The family's stored filter for one child: the level, the categories they switched on, the allow and block lists, the keyword dictionary, and the temporary allows that are open at this minute. The temporary allows are computed from their own end times rather than stored as open, so nothing has to remember to close them. Guardians only: a child membership cannot be proven to be the subject of this read.

200.description: The server's policy, with the allows open right now.

patch.summary: Switches categories on or off, and edits the two lists
patch.description: Only the fields that are sent change; the rest keep what the family already chose. A category key the server does not know is refused rather than stored, because a switch that does nothing while looking like it does something is the failure this wave exists to prevent. A host cannot be on both lists: the engine resolves the block list first, so an allow entry that is also blocked would be a line on a screen with no effect.

200.description: The policy as stored, after the change.

409.description: The policy changed since this screen read it (`web_filter_stale_version`), or a host was sent on both lists (`web_filter_host_both_lists`).

get.summary: What this child would get if they opened this host
get.description: The father's preview, answered by the same decision function the handset applies and in the same order: block list, then an open temporary allow, then the allow list, then the keyword dictionary, then the category, then allow. A preview produced by different rules than the filter would be a screen that disagrees with the phone in a child's hand. It decides nothing and stores nothing.

200.description: The decision, its source, and the policy version it came from.

get.summary: The doors that were opened, and whether they are still open
get.description: Every request this child has made or been given, newest first, each carrying its computed state: `pending`, `active`, `expired` or `denied`. An approval is stored with the minute it closes at, so `expired` is an answer about the clock rather than a status somebody has to write.

200.description: The requests, and the hosts open right now.

post.summary: A child asks for one host, for a stated number of minutes
post.description: A guardian may ask on a child's behalf - a child who speaks rather than taps still gets a record - and the child's own handset asks through its device credential on the device route. Only one open question per child and host exists at a time; a second one is refused rather than stacked, so the guardians answer a question instead of a queue.

201.description: The question, open and waiting.

409.description: This host is already waiting for an answer (`web_filter_request_pending`).

post.summary: Approve a door or refuse it
post.description: Approve opens the host until a stated minute; the granted minutes are the guardian's decision, may be fewer than the child asked for, and can never exceed the request - quietly widening a question is not answering it. Deny opens nothing. An answered question cannot be answered again: a second answer would either extend a door nobody re-asked for or refuse something already open.

200.description: The request as answered.

404.description: No such request in this family (`web_filter_request_not_found`).

409.description: Already answered (`web_filter_request_decided`) or the grant exceeded the request (`web_filter_grant_exceeds_request`).

post.summary: The handset itself asks for one host
post.description: The device credential is the asker, which is why this path carries no child id: the credential proves which child is speaking, and a parameter a client can choose would prove nothing. The question lands in the same inbox the family already answers, through the same operation as a guardian's request.

201.description: The question, open and waiting.

403.description: The device credential is not accepted (`device_credential_rejected`).

409.description: This host is already waiting for an answer (`web_filter_request_pending`).

get.summary: The policy this handset must apply, and the doors that are open
get.description: Read through the device credential, so a handset can only ever fetch the policy of the child it was paired with. The same rows a guardian reads, produced by the same functions: the phone in a child's hand and the screen in a parent's hand are never shown two different filters.

200.description: The server's policy for this device's child.

403.description: The device credential is not accepted (`device_credential_rejected`).

post.summary: A handset testifies about its own protection plane
post.description: Append-only: every report is kept forever, so a family asking "when did this start?" gets an answer instead of the newest row. `observed_at` is kept as the handset's testimony of when it looked, while how old a report is is measured from the moment the SERVER heard it - a device clock is the first thing someone with something to hide would move. The response carries the health the family is shown, computed from this report and the clock.

201.description: The report as stored, and the computed health.

403.description: The device credential is not accepted (`device_credential_rejected`).

422.description: An observation this server does not know (`web_filter_observation_unknown`).

get.summary: Whether protection is actually on, device by device
get.description: The state a family reads is computed from each device's newest report and the clock, never stored. A device that has never reported, or has not reported within the freshness window, is `unverified` - not `protected`, because nothing recently said so, and not `at_risk`, because nothing said that either. Silence is not health, and this read is where that law is kept.

200.description: Every device in the family with its computed state, and the counts.

get.summary: What this child has to do, each task with its open cycle
get.description: The tasks a guardian stated for one child, newest first, each carrying the claim currently open on it. A task nobody has said anything about returns `claim: null` rather than a default, because "not claimed yet" and "claimed" are different sentences and a screen must be able to say which.

200.description: This child's tasks.

post.summary: States a task and the points it is worth
post.description: The number of points is stated here, once, by a guardian. It becomes a property of the task rather than of the confirmation that follows, so the party being rewarded can never name the size of the reward. A task is archived rather than deleted when it is withdrawn: the ledger entries it produced keep pointing at the statement that produced them.

201.description: The task as stored.

422.description: The title is empty or too long, or the points are outside 1-200 or not whole.

post.summary: Marks a task as done on the child's behalf
post.description: For a child who spoke to a guardian instead of tapping their own handset. The claim is recorded with its author, and it is not an achievement: no points move until a guardian confirms. Exactly one claim may be open on a task at a time - the second press is refused rather than queued.

201.description: The claim as recorded, waiting for a guardian.

404.description: The task does not exist, or it is not this child's task.

409.description: A claim is already waiting on this task (`task_claim_pending`), or the task was withdrawn (`task_archived`).

post.summary: Confirms a claim, and the points become real - or declines it, and nothing does
post.description: The guardian's word is what turns a claim into points. There is deliberately no `points` field in this request: the reward was stated on the task, and this call copies it. A confirmation writes exactly one append-only ledger entry, and the database refuses a second entry for the same claim, so a retried request cannot pay twice. A decline awards nothing - not less, not a negative - and leaves the task open so the child can try again.

200.description: The task with its answered cycle, and the balance as a sum over the ledger.

404.description: The task does not exist, or it is not this child's task.

409.description: No claim is waiting (`task_claim_not_pending`), the claim was already answered (`task_claim_already_answered`), or this claim already produced its entry (`task_already_confirmed`).

get.summary: The child's balance, and the entries that produced it
get.description: A balance is a sum, computed on every read from an append-only ledger - there is no stored counter to drift away from the record. The entries travel with the number so that "40 points" can always be answered with "confirmed by whom, and when".

200.description: The balance and its entries.

get.summary: The child's own tasks and balance, read by their handset
get.description: One read, because on that phone it is one screen: what I have to do, what is waiting for a parent, and what I have earned. There is no child id in the path - the credential issued at pairing is what proves which child is asking.

200.description: This handset's tasks and points.

post.summary: "I did it", from the handset itself
post.description: The child marks their own task as done. The claim waits for a guardian exactly as a spoken one does - the same table, the same rules, and the same single pending claim per task. Nothing about pressing this button awards points.

201.description: The claim as recorded, waiting for a guardian.

409.description: A claim is already waiting on this task (`task_claim_pending`), or the task was withdrawn (`task_archived`).

get.summary: The conversations this guardian is in
get.description: Every room the caller is a participant of, with its participants, its newest message, how many unread messages it holds and how many other participants have read that newest message. A guardian is not shown a room they are not in: the read joins on the caller's own member row, so "not in the room" is not a filter that could be forgotten.

200.description: The rooms this participant is in, most recently active first.

post.summary: Creates a direct conversation or a user-created group
post.description: The creator names each peer explicitly from the server-owned family participant roster. No guardian is added automatically unless the active server collaboration policy requires it. Direct conversations name exactly one peer; groups name at least two. The server validates every participant against the same family and applies the configured group-size and child-safety rules.

201.description: The room as stored, with its participants.

post.summary: Adds one participant to a conversation
post.description: Adds a same-family active guardian or child to a group. Direct conversations remain pairs, and only a caller already in the group may manage its membership. If the active safety policy requires guardian inclusion when a child is added, the server applies that rule before committing.

200.description: The room with its participants after the addition.

get.summary: What was said in a conversation, from after a sequence number
get.description: Messages are ordered by the server's own sequence number, never by a client clock. A deleted message is returned as a tombstone: its sequence and the trace of who deleted it survive while the text does not. `readCount` counts other participants who have marked themselves read up to a message - the author is never counted, and no delivery is ever claimed.

parameters.name: afterSeq
parameters.description: Return messages after this sequence number. The incremental read: without a push transport a client asks for what it has not seen.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many messages to return, oldest first after `afterSeq`. At most 200.

200.description: A page of messages, oldest first, with the caller's own read state.

post.summary: Says something in a conversation
post.description: The author is the caller's own membership; no field in this request names an author, so no request can speak as somebody else. The sequence number is allocated from the thread's own counter inside this transaction. A resend carrying the same `clientMessageId` returns the message that already exists, with the sequence it already has, and is not an error.

201.description: The stored message, and whether this was a resend.

patch.summary: Changes a message you wrote, stating the revision you read
patch.description: Only the author edits their own words. The edit states the revision it read, the body it replaced is kept in the revisions table, and `revision` and `editedAt` move together - a reader can always see that a message changed and when. A deleted message is not edited.

200.description: The message as it now stands.

post.summary: Deletes a message you wrote, keeping the trace
post.description: Only the author deletes their own words - a guardian deleting a child's message would be rewriting the child. The body and the stored earlier versions are removed, while the row, its sequence and who deleted it when remain: a hole in the numbering would make the thread untrustworthy, and a product that keeps the text has not deleted anything.

200.description: The deleted message: its sequence and its trace, without its text.

post.summary: States how far you have read
post.description: A participant's own statement about themselves, which is the only kind of receipt this surface accepts. The mark cannot pass the newest message in the thread, and it only ever moves forward, so a stale client cannot un-read anything.

200.description: The caller's read state after the mark.

get.summary: The conversations this child is in, from their own handset
get.description: No child id is taken from the request: the credential issued at pairing is what proves which child is asking, so a handset cannot list a sibling's rooms even by guessing. The rooms are the ones whose member rows name this child.

200.description: The rooms this child is in, most recently active first.

post.summary: Creates a direct conversation or user-created group from a paired child device
post.description: The creator is the child identified by the protected device credential. Every selected peer is validated against the same family roster. The active server policy decides whether the child may create this kind and whether guardians must be included; the client cannot override those rules.

201.description: The created conversation.

get.summary: What was said in a room, from the child's own handset
get.description: The member row that must exist is the child's own, so a handset reads only the conversations that name its child. Messages are ordered by the server's sequence and a deleted message keeps its place as a tombstone.

parameters.name: afterSeq
parameters.description: Return messages after this sequence number. The incremental read: without a push transport a client asks for what it has not seen.

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: How many messages to return, oldest first after `afterSeq`. At most 200.

200.description: A page of messages, oldest first, with the child's own read state.

post.summary: The child says something, from their own handset
post.description: The author is the child the credential proves, never a child id typed into a body, and the room must already name that child. The sequence is the server's, and a resend of the same `clientMessageId` is the same message.

201.description: The stored message, and whether this was a resend.

post.summary: The child states how far they have read
post.description: The child's own read mark, from the handset that proves which child they are. It cannot pass the newest message and it only moves forward.

200.description: The child's read state after the mark.

patch.summary: The child changes a message they wrote
patch.description: Same law as the guardian surface and the same author check: the handset writes as its own child, so a message somebody else wrote is refused with `chat_not_author`. The edit states the revision it read and keeps the body it replaced.

200.description: The message as it now stands.

post.summary: The child deletes a message they wrote
post.description: Only the author deletes their own words, on this surface too: the handset proves which child it is, and a message that child did not write is refused. The trace survives the text and the sequence keeps its place.

200.description: The deleted message: its sequence and its trace, without its text.

get.summary: The active participants available for a family conversation
get.description: Returns only same-family active guardian memberships and children, with safe display fields. Account subjects, contact details and device credentials are never included.

200.description: The server-owned participant roster.

get.summary: Reads server-enforced family collaboration rules
get.description: Returns the persisted policy or the safe default. The defaults do not add guardians automatically. Roles and child-safety controls are enforced by server operations, not trusted from the client.

200.description: The active collaboration policy.

patch.summary: Updates collaboration rules as the primary guardian
patch.description: Applies one or more collaboration controls with optimistic version checking. Only the primary guardian may change policy; role delegation is restricted to guardian roles, and the server continues to protect child, device, identity, location and emergency capabilities.

200.description: The updated policy.

get.summary: The active family participants available to this child device
get.description: The paired device identity is derived from its credential. The returned roster is family-bound and omits account subjects, contact details and device secrets.

200.description: The server-owned participant roster.

post.summary: Adds a peer to a group from the paired child device
post.description: The child may manage group membership only when the primary guardian enabled that server policy. Direct conversations cannot be expanded. The new participant reads from the next message sequence and cannot see earlier conversation history.

200.description: The group with its active participants.

oidcBearer.description: Issuer, audience, signature and subject are verified server-side. Provider selection is not represented in this contract.

deviceCredential.name: Authorization
deviceCredential.description: One-time paired child-device capability in the form Device token. It is stored only in Android Keystore, not as a guardian bearer token.

IdempotencyKey.name: Idempotency-Key
IdempotencyKey.description: Unique per operation intent. Reusing it with different intent is rejected.

AppId.name: appId
AppId.description: The app as the handset names it: a package-style identifier such as `com.example.game`.

RequestId.name: requestId
RequestId.description: The temporary-allow request this decision answers.

EventId.name: eventId
EventId.description: The event a guardian stated for the family.

InvalidRequest.description: Malformed JSON, identifier or input contract.

AuthenticationRequired.description: Missing, invalid, expired or otherwise unverifiable OIDC bearer token.

FamilyAccessDenied.description: No permitted active family membership for the requested action.

Forbidden.description: Verified principal lacks the exact required authority.

NotFound.description: Requested resource was not found within the authorized path.

Conflict.description: State, idempotency, continuity, expiry or lifecycle conflict.

RateLimited.description: The verified principal exceeded the protected API request allowance. Respect the standard RateLimit response header before retrying.

ServiceNotReady.description: Configuration, database or reviewed schema is not ready for protected operations.

credentialState.description: unclaimed means a guardian registered the device but no handset has claimed a pairing yet.

FamilyDevice.description: A linked device as the guardian reads it. The flat facts are the stored row; capabilities and health are derived server-side by device-lifecycle.js on every read and never stored, so a client renders the server's answer instead of recomputing whether a child is protected. `version` is the row's own version for optimistic concurrency, which is why it is an integer here while GuardianDeviceLifecycle publishes the contract version as a string.

role.description: Display-only current role. The API remains the authorization authority.

correlationId.description: Server-generated linkage for newer audit/outbox evidence. Historical entries can be null.

expiresAt.description: Short-lived explanation window. Authority is re-resolved from the server, never extended from this document.

confidence.description: Observed facts are certain (1). Suggestions, admitted in a later version, must carry their own confidence and a reject path.

reasonCode.description: Closed vocabulary, enforced here, in the operation and by the database. Omitted or null means the guardian did not classify the loss.

DeviceCapability.description: What a device can currently do, decided by the server. The client renders this and never recomputes it, so the two cannot disagree about whether a child is protected.

reasonCode.description: A machine reason code. The server ships no prose, so no English can leak into an Arabic screen; the client owns the sentence.

needsAttention.description: True only for revoked, never_reported, stale and offline. A healthy device produces nothing on the guardian surface, by construction.

GuardianDeviceLifecycle.description: A device as the guardian is allowed to see it, derived server-side from the stored row. Capability and health are never stored: a stored copy of a derived fact is a second version of the truth waiting to disagree with the first.

credentialState.description: unclaimed means a guardian registered the device but no handset has claimed a pairing.

role.description: Membership role as stored. A caller renders it with its own vocabulary.

statusReasonCode.description: Machine code recorded when the membership stopped being active.

isSelf.description: Decided on the server against the authenticated principal. Never inferred by the client.

GeoCoordinates.description: WGS84 degrees. Ranges are validated by the request schema and again by the database.

radiusMeters.description: Between 50 m and 50 km, enforced by the request schema and by migration 102.

vertices.description: Ordered ring. The first point is not repeated at the end; containment closes it.

SafeZoneGeometry.description: Both shapes are first-class, and exactly one is carried. A circle missing its radius is not a circle with a default radius.

childIds.description: The children this zone is evaluated for. Never empty.

alertEnter.description: Whether an arrival is announced. A crossing is still recorded when this is false.

alertExit.description: Whether a departure is announced. A crossing is still recorded when this is false.

version.description: Increases when the shape or its flags change. A crossing records the version it was judged against.

LocationFixRequest.description: The acquisition state is an honesty switch: located and stale_last_known must carry latitude, longitude and accuracyMeters; acquiring and unavailable must carry none of the three. A coordinate of zero is a real place in the Atlantic, so "no position" is expressed by absence and never by a placeholder.

fixId.description: Chosen once by the device for this report. It is the row identity, so the same fix can never be stored twice.

integritySoftWarning.description: A soft signal for a guardian. It is never a score, never a verdict, and never proof of tampering.

recordedAt.description: The device clock. Kept separate from the server clock: a handset with a wrong time is an operational fact, not something to silently rewrite.

baseline.description: True when this is the first observation of the state rather than an observed crossing. It is recorded and NOT announced.

notified.description: Whether the zone flags asked for this transition to be announced. False for a baseline crossing even when the flag is on.

evaluated.description: False when the fix was stored without being judged against any boundary.

reason.description: Why the fix was or was not evaluated. Duplicate also sets replayed, and the crossings listed are the ones already recorded for this fix rather than new ones.

replayed.description: True when this fix id had already been stored. No second row and no second crossing exists.

pruned.description: Trail samples deleted by the retention window inside this same transaction.

state.description: live: reported within the liveness window. silent: reported before and has stopped. never: has not reported since it was linked. A device that stopped reporting and one that never started are different answers.

observedCrossing.description: False when the state comes from a baseline observation rather than from a crossing anybody watched happen.

visibility.description: Who may read this surface: every active member of the family, with no privileged viewer.
The rule this read obeys: every active member of the family sees the same rows.

retentionDays.description: How long a fix survives. Older fixes are deleted inside the same transaction that records a newer one.

SosLocationClass.description: The honesty switch of the press. `ready` and `stale_last_known` carry a position and the accuracy it came with; `acquiring` and `unavailable` carry no coordinates at all. A press that names a place nobody measured sends a family to the wrong door.

SosConnectionClass.description: How the handset could reach the network when the button was pressed.

SosTerminalReason.description: Why the incident ended. A closed incident with no reason explains nothing.

SosDeliveryState.description: What the platform can honestly claim it did. `recorded` means a durable payload was written for a transport to pick up; `not_configured` means there was nothing to send it on, and `reasonCode` says why. There is deliberately no `delivered` state: nothing in this repository can send a push or a text message, and a parent told "sent" when nobody sent anything stops checking.

SosAlertPicture.description: The picture as it was at press time, stored rather than recomputed: the only honest answer to "where was she when she pressed it" is the answer that was true then.

fixId.description: The trail sample this press points at, when the handset had one. The crossing table and this one keep a fix that an incident refers to from being pruned.

reasonCode.description: Present exactly when the state is not_configured.

raisedByKind.description: Which door the press came through. Derived from it, never stated by the caller.

open.description: True while the incident is not resolved. Everything that is still true of it is still visible.

resolvedByKind.description: Who closed it. A handset may only close its own child's incident, and only as a false alarm, so the difference between the two matters after the fact.

SosAlertRaiseRequest.description: The press, with the picture the handset had at that moment. The picture travels with the press instead of being looked up afterwards, and the same coordinate law as a location fix applies: a place requires its accuracy, and "no position" is expressed by absence.

panicQuiet.description: The preference captured at press time, never re-read later.

fixId.description: The trail sample the press points at, when the handset had one.

pressedAt.description: Optional: a handset that was offline reports the press when it can. Absent means the server's own clock.

SosAlertResolveRequest.description: A handset may only close its own child's incident as a false alarm; a guardian states any of the three reasons.

replayed.description: True when the answer reports an incident that already was in this state, so a retry cannot be mistaken for a new act.

eligibleContacts.description: Verified and enabled contacts the escalation reached.

skippedUnverified.description: Contacts the family added but has not verified. Reported rather than silently dropped: a parent must find this out now, not on the day it was needed.

verification.description: Only a verified contact ever escalates - the same hard-skip law the client's escalation resolver enforces.

SosBackupContactCreateRequest.description: A new rung is always created unverified: a number that verifies itself on the way in is a number nobody checked. Verifying it is a separate act.

archived.description: Takes the contact off the ladder without erasing the fact that it was once on it.

reasonCode.description: Why the answer is what it is. Null means nothing is in the way. The vocabulary is closed and shared by the state and every app decision, so a screen never has to interpret a free-form string.

date.description: Today, in the family's own offset.

weekday.description: ISO weekday, 1 = Monday in the family's own offset.

capMinutes.description: The daily cap, or null when the family set none.

configured.description: False until a guardian saves a policy. The defaults are published either way, so a screen never invents them.

dailyLimitMinutes.description: 0 means no cap for the day.

expectedVersion.description: The version this screen read. A mismatch is a 409, never a silent overwrite.

openRequest.description: The question waiting for a parent right now, if there is one.

reasonCode.description: Why the answer is what it is. Null means nothing is in the way. The vocabulary is closed and shared by the state and every app decision, so a screen never has to interpret a free-form string.

knownOnDevice.description: True when a handset reported it. A rule for an app nobody has is still a family's decision.

countable.description: Whether its minutes count against the daily cap.

rule.description: Null means nobody has decided: the app is pending.

unlimited.description: Only with `allowed`. Lets an app bypass the daily cap without unblocking it.

usageDate.description: The day the granted minutes belong to.

grantedMinutes.description: Approval only, and never more than the child asked for. Defaults to the amount requested.

usage.description: Cumulative minutes per app for a day. The server keeps the greater of this and what it stored.

date.description: Today or the day before, in the family's own clock.

apps.description: What is installed, as the handset names it. An app nobody has ruled on becomes pending.

request.description: The child's question, if the phone is asking for more minutes in this same call.

reportedRequest.description: The question this call raised or found, so a phone knows its ask was recorded.

WebFilterCategoryKey.description: The six categories a family can switch on. The same six are declared in the client's `WebFilterCategories.known`, and a test compares the two lists: a toggle the server does not accept would be a switch that does nothing.

WebFilterTempAllowState.description: Computed from the stored status and the clock. `expired` is never stored: an approval carries the minute it closes at, so it closes by itself.

ProtectionHealthState.description: `unverified` is a first-class answer: a device that has not reported lately is neither claimed safe nor called broken. `protected` is only ever produced by a recent report that said so.

level.description: A preset that seeds the categories when chosen; what is enforced afterwards is always `enabledCategories`.

allowHosts.description: Hosts this child may open even when a category would refuse them.

blockHosts.description: Hosts refused before anything else, including a temporary allow.

activeTempAllows.description: Hosts a guardian opened for a stated time, computed against the clock at this read.

version.description: Increases with every save. A screen sends the version it read and is refused if the policy moved underneath it.

WebFilterPolicyUpdateRequest.description: Every field optional: flipping one switch must not reset the other five. Lists are replaced rather than merged, because removing a host has to be possible.

blockHosts.description: Replaces the block list. A host on both lists is refused.

expectedVersion.description: The version the screen read. Zero means "never saved", and is a real value rather than a sentinel.

denySource.description: Null when allowed. The source is stated rather than implied, so the child block page and the parent preview describe the same refusal the same way.

normalizedHost.description: The host as the engine read it: lower case, no scheme, no port, no leading `www.`.

status.description: What was stored. What a screen shows is `state`.

grantedMinutes.description: The guardian's answer, never more than was asked. Null until answered, and on a denial.

expiresAt.description: Always present on an approval, always null on a denial: a denial opens nothing.

grantedMinutes.description: Optional on an approve: fewer minutes than asked is an answer, more is refused.

activeHosts.description: The hosts open at this minute.

observedState.description: What the handset saw. `healthy` is a claim like any other and is stored as the handset's claim; the server decides what the family is told by reading it with the clock in hand.

observedAt.description: The handset's own stamp, kept as testimony. Freshness is measured against the server's receipt time instead.

reportedAt.description: When the server heard it. This is the anchor freshness is measured from.

freshnessMinutes.description: How long a report speaks for. Beyond it a device reads as `unverified`.

title.description: What the child is asked to do.

note.description: What "done" means, if a word is needed.

points.description: What this task is worth. Stated once, by a guardian.

audienceThreadId.description: Optional direct/group conversation. The creator and beneficiary must be active members; other child members can see the task but only the designated child can claim it.

note.description: What the child says they did. Nothing is required here: a claim is a claim.
Why. For a decline this is read by a child, so it is worth a sentence.

TaskDecisionRequest.description: Note what is absent: no number of points. The reward is a property of the task, and this request cannot restate it.

claimedByDeviceId.description: Set when the child's own handset spoke.

claimedByMembershipId.description: Set when a guardian spoke for the child.

pointsAwarded.description: Copied from the task at the moment of confirmation. Null on a decline, always.

claim.description: The cycle currently open on this task, or null when nobody has said anything.

audienceThreadId.description: Optional direct/group conversation used as the server-enforced visibility and notification-routing scope.

points.description: Positive in this wave. A spending reason will arrive as its own named entry, not as a negative award.
A sum over the ledger, computed on every read.

awarded.description: The entry this confirmation wrote, or null on a decline.

FamilyEventResponseRecord.description: One child's answer, with the author who gave it. Exactly one of the two author fields is present: a handset cannot answer for a family member, and a guardian cannot hide behind a handset.

FamilyEventAttendanceRecord.description: What a person recorded about what happened, and who recorded it. Never inferred from a device.

FamilyEventAudienceEntry.description: One invited child, with their answer and what was recorded about their attendance. Both are absent until they exist - never defaulted.

FamilyEvent.description: A family event. `version` rises on every change: an edit must state the version it read, so two guardians editing the same evening collide loudly instead of silently overwriting each other. A cancelled event keeps its times, its audience and its answers, and gains the author, the reason and the moment of the cancellation.

reminderMinutes.description: A recorded preference. This contract does not claim a notification was delivered.

audienceThreadId.description: Optional direct/group conversation used as the routing scope. Child invitees remain explicit event-audience records.

endsAt.description: Must be after `startsAt`, and no more than a month after it.

childIds.description: Optional explicit child audience. If omitted or empty, audienceThreadId must name a direct/group conversation; its current child participants are snapshotted as invitees.

audienceThreadId.description: Optional same-family direct/group conversation; must be paired with active creator membership. If childIds is empty, current child participants become invitees.

version.description: The version the client read. A mismatch is a 409, not a merge.

childIds.description: Optional replacement audience. If omitted with audienceThreadId, the group’s current child participants are used.

audienceThreadId.description: Replace or clear the event’s direct/group routing scope. Setting null keeps the explicit child audience unless childIds is also supplied.

reason.description: Why the plan changed. A cancellation a child cannot understand is worse than the cancellation itself.

DeviceEvent.description: One child's own view: the event they are invited to, their own answer, and what was recorded about their attendance. Deliberately without any sibling's answer.

ChatParticipant.description: One participant of a conversation. A guardian is identified by their membership and role; a child by their name. The OIDC subject of a membership is deliberately absent: a chat list has no use for a durable identifier for a person.

displayName.description: The child's name, for a child participant.

isSelf.description: True for the caller's own membership row; decided on the server, never guessed by a client.

ChatMessage.description: One message in a conversation. A deleted message keeps its sequence number and its trace while its text is gone, so the numbering stays trustworthy and the family knows something was said and removed.

seq.description: Allocated by the server from the thread's own counter inside the sending transaction; never supplied by a client.

body.description: The text, or null for a deleted message.

revision.description: 1 until the message is edited; every edit moves it and `editedAt` together.

readCount.description: How many OTHER participants have marked themselves read up to this message. The author is never counted, and nothing here claims a delivery.

ChatThread.description: A conversation, with only participants the caller may see and the newest message. `lastReadSeq` and `unreadCount` are the caller’s own state.

kind.description: New conversations are direct or user-created groups; family/child remain readable legacy kinds.

lastReadSeq.description: How far the CALLER has read; a participant's own statement, which only ever moves forward.

unreadCount.description: Messages after the caller's read mark that somebody else wrote.

ChatReadState.description: One participant's own read mark. There is no endpoint that states it for somebody else, and no read mark is inferred from a device being online.

hasMore.description: True when the page was full, so the caller can ask for what follows with `afterSeq`.

ChatMessageSendResponse.description: A send, and whether it was a resend: the same `clientMessageId` from the same author returns the message that already exists, with the sequence it already has, rather than a second copy.

ChatThreadCreateRequest.description: A new direct or group conversation. `participants` contains explicit other family-member references; the server adds the creator and only adds guardians if an active safety policy requires it.

participants.description: For direct, exactly one peer. For group, two or more peers. All IDs are checked against the server-owned family roster.

ChatThreadMemberRequest.description: One active family participant to add to a group. Direct conversations remain a pair; legacy thread kinds remain readable but are not expanded to new child conversations.

ChatMessageSendRequest.description: What was said. There is no author field: the author is decided by how the request arrived - a paired handset writes as its own child, an authenticated person as their membership.

clientMessageId.description: The sender's own name for this message. A resend with the same value returns the same message instead of a second one.

revision.description: The revision the author read. A mismatch is refused rather than silently overwriting words somebody else already saw.

readSeq.description: How far this participant has read. It cannot pass the newest message in the thread, and it only ever moves forward.

transport.description: The active delivery transport. The current service uses polling; SSE and WebSockets are reserved for a future verified implementation.

contentTypes.description: Message media types the active server implementation accepts. The current service advertises text/plain only; adding media types requires a verified server and client implementation.

serverSentEvents.description: Whether server-sent event streaming is implemented and available. The current service returns false; a future implementation may advertise true only after its safety and delivery behavior are verified.

webSockets.description: Whether websocket transport is implemented and available. The current service returns false; a future implementation may advertise true only after its safety and delivery behavior are verified.

attachments.description: Whether file attachments is implemented and available. The current service returns false; a future implementation may advertise true only after its safety and delivery behavior are verified.

audio.description: Whether voice and audio messages is implemented and available. The current service returns false; a future implementation may advertise true only after its safety and delivery behavior are verified.

presence.description: Whether participant presence states is implemented and available. The current service returns false; a future implementation may advertise true only after its safety and delivery behavior are verified.

richReactions.description: Whether rich reactions and message-state interactions is implemented and available. The current service returns false; a future implementation may advertise true only after its safety and delivery behavior are verified.

FamilyCollaborationPolicyUpdateRequest.description: Partial policy update. Only the primary guardian may write; child and protected capabilities cannot be delegated.
